🪶 Poetry Corner

Robert W. Service (1874–1958)

AI voice reading, not a recording of Robert Service. Photograph of Robert W. Service, public domain.
🖍️ Highlighter: tap the line that sets the Wild against everything before it.
The Call of the Wild
Robert W. Service (1907) · from “The Call of the Wild,” stanza 5, lines 1–8
· · ·
They have cradled you in custom, they have primed you with their preaching, They have soaked you in convention through and through; They have put you in a showcase; you're a credit to their teaching— But can't you hear the Wild?—it's calling you. Let us probe the silent places, let us seek what luck betide us; Let us journey to a lonely land I know. There's a whisper on the night-wind, there's a star agleam to guide us, And the Wild is calling, calling... let us go.
· · ·
2In Buck’s story, what is the “showcase”?
cradled you in custom: raised you inside habits and rules · primed: filled up ahead of time · convention: the usual, accepted way of doing things · showcase: a glass case for showing off fine things · betide: happen to · agleam: shining

⚖️ Strong or Weak?
Four reflection sentences from other students
0 / 4

Read each sentence. Does it only describe the project, or does it explain the change?

1“Putting the warm estate on one side and the wolf pack on the other shows that the wild did not break Buck. It freed the strong creature the comfortable house never asked him to be.”
2“On the left I put a house and a sunny yard, and on the right I put snow, trees, and five gray wolves.”
3“I put Buck in front of the pack instead of inside it, which felt important to me.”
4“My first label calls Buck ‘a king who has never been afraid,’ and my second calls him ‘a creature who answers a call older than people,’ which is how I show what the wild wakes up in him.”
📜 Your answers in words (goes into your Week 6 PDF)

Rubric self-check
Understanding of the text: I can point to the lines in my essay that show I read the book closely.
Reasoning and evidence: I can point to where my evidence proves my thesis.
Clarity and precision: I can point to my clearest paragraph and my best-edited sentence.
Intellectual honesty: every idea is mine or clearly the novel’s, and every quotation is copied exactly.
